A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Gaussian Mixture Flow Matching Models and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–E. The complete material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Sections 4.1–4.2 report original checkerboard and ImageNet experiments. Appendix B.3 also reports CIFAR-10 results from a GMFlow model trained from scratch, distinguishing these from sourced comparator results.

after.justification: v3 retains the original checkerboard, ImageNet, and CIFAR-10 experiments, including quantitative results, ablations, and generated samples in the main text and Appendix B.

M1.justification: The model, losses, guidance, spectral sampling, and solver procedures are retained. Appendix D.2 repairs algebraic expansions of existing operations. Algorithm 2 replaces the denominator τ with σ_τ, which is equivalent under the retained schedule σ_t = t.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate 2D checkerboard sampling, class-conditioned ImageNet 256×256 generation, and unconditional CIFAR-10 generation in Appendix B.3. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within corresponding experiments. ImageNet retains DDPM, Euler, DPM++, DEIS, UniPC, and SA-Solver comparisons; Table 5 retains DDPM, SN-DDPM, and GMS for CIFAR-10.

E3.justification: Sections 4 and Appendix A retain the same architectures, training budgets, guidance sweeps, sampling-step and sub-step settings, and evaluation metrics. The NLL evaluation still uses 50K training samples; no new evaluation protocol is introduced.

E4.justification: The component-count and solver analyses, distribution-conversion ablation in Figure 3, ImageNet design ablations in Table 4, and sub-step analysis in Appendix B.1/Figure 10 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed-based variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Both retain the same point-estimate reporting practices.

E6.justification: Numerical results, plotted findings, and qualitative samples match. Table 2 retains GM-SDE 2 Precision of 0.950 at NFE 32 with orthogonal projection; Table 5 retains its CIFAR-10 FIDs of 9.11, 4.16, 3.79, and 3.76 at NFE 10, 25, 50, and 100.

T1.justification: Appendix C.1 corrects the score-function sign. Appendix D.2 changes Eq. (47) from (Σ + Σ_k)^−1 to (Σ^−1 + Σ_k^−1)^−1 and inserts the missing inverse in Eq. (50). Section 3.1 also changes the categorical special-case condition from s → 0 to s ≈ 0. These are localized mathematical corrections; the main theorem and proof remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and performance claims: Gaussian-mixture flow modeling, analytic SDE/ODE solvers, probabilistic guidance reducing over-saturation, and improved generation quality.

C2.justification: Interpretations of component count, solver behavior, guidance, and spectral sampling are retained. Both versions state the same limitation that pixel-wise factorization may not fully exploit GMFlow's potential.

D1.justification: Implementation and reproduction information remains unchanged, including Appendix A's hyperparameters, solver adaptations, guidance grids, and training on 16 A100 GPUs for 200K iterations. The repository link and reported inference timing are also retained.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged. Sadat et al. is updated from a 2024 preprint to ICLR 2025, and two bibliographic URLs are removed; these are metadata edits rather than changes in related-work coverage.

P1.justification: Localized edits standardize solver and pseudocode notation, clarify 'flow matching' terminology in Table 6, correct contact and acknowledgment text, and update bibliography metadata. The section organization and narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 6 gains increased row spacing and adjusted column placement. References reflow and the pseudocode layout shifts slightly. Figures and experimental tables retain their content, structure, and placement.

improvement.justification: v3 fixes the erroneous score sign and missing matrix inverses in Appendices C.1 and D.2, improving mathematical consistency and reducing potential implementation errors. Notation cleanup and the more spacious Table 6 also improve readability. These are useful, localized improvements; the method, empirical evidence, and central claims remain unchanged.
